message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to not talk to Lois last time I saw her. Let me start by understanding the situation better. Lois has been going through a tough time since her husband passed away, and I usually make an effort to talk to her when I see her. But last time, she was talking with a couple of other people, so I waved and gestured for her to call me instead of approaching her directly. Hmm, so why did I do that? Maybe I thought that since she was already engaged in a conversation, it wasn't the best time to interrupt. I didn't want to seem rude or intrusive. Plus, I wanted to give her some space, especially considering she's been through a difficult time. By waving and gesturing, I was still acknowledging her presence and letting her know I was there, but I wasn't forcing her to interact with me at that moment. But is that the right approach? On one hand, I'm respecting her space and not interrupting her conversation. On the other hand, maybe she would have appreciated me taking the initiative to talk to her, especially since she's been going through a tough time. I don't want her to feel neglected or like I'm avoiding her. I also need to consider how Lois might feel about this. If she's grieving, she might appreciate the space, or she might want more support from others. It's possible that she was talking to others because she was seeking comfort or distraction, and I didn't want to interfere with that. But it's also possible that she would have liked me to reach out more actively. Another thing to think about is the context of our relationship. Are we close friends, or are we more acquaintances? If we're close, she might expect more from me, whereas if we're acquaintances, she might understand that I'm giving her space. Also, cultural factors might play a role. In some cultures, it's more common to give people space when they're grieving, while in others, reaching out more actively is expected. I also need to reflect on my own intentions. Was I avoiding her because I felt uncomfortable or because I genuinely thought it was better to give her space? If it was the former, then maybe I should work on being more comfortable in these situations. If it was the latter, then perhaps my approach was appropriate. Additionally, I should consider the long-term implications of my actions. If I consistently avoid talking to Lois when she's with others, she might start to feel isolated or like I'm not interested in supporting her. On the other hand, if I always approach her when I see her, she might feel overwhelmed or like she doesn't have a choice in whether to interact with me. Maybe a better approach would be to find a balance. I could still acknowledge her presence, like I did by waving, but also make an effort to talk to her when it seems appropriate. Perhaps I could approach her after she's finished talking to the others, or find a time when she's alone to have a more meaningful conversation. I also wonder if there are other ways I can support Lois besides just talking to her in person. Maybe I could send her a message or call her to check in, or offer to help her with something practical. That way, I'm still showing that I care without necessarily interrupting her when she's with others. In summary, I think my initial approach of waving and gesturing was considerate, but I should also make an effort to talk to Lois when it seems appropriate. It's important to balance respecting her space with showing that I care and am willing to support her during this difficult time.
